pageCache.pageTitle: Bloxham Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to our school. I hope that our website gives you a sense of what it is like to be a member of our school family.
At Bloxham Church of England Primary School, each and every child is valued for who they are, with their well-being and sense of worth being key. Our mission is for our pupils to feel good enough, deserving, confident in themselves, loved and cared for.
Our vision is for our school to become central to its diverse community, for all members to feel included, valued and treated equitably. We believe that in nurturing and supporting our pupils, we encourage them to feel safe, enabling them to be curious to learn, ambitious to succeed and have the confidence to be creative.
As the school community, we all have a common goal to ensure our school is the very best it can be, that our children are happy, love school, thrive and leave our school as well-rounded individuals ready to face the challenges ahead. As such, we must be role models for our children and every day, through our actions and behaviours, live up to our school Christian values.
The best gift you are ever going to give someone – the permission to feel safe in their own skin. To feel worthy. To feel they are enough.
- Hannah Brencher, educator and TED speaker
Sarah Marshall, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Bloxham Church of England Primary School - SMSC & Bloxham's Cultural Passport
pageCache.text:
SMSC & Bloxham's Cultural Passport
During a child's time at our school, we hope to provide them with a range of additional experiences which will enhance their learning, provide lasting memories and develop a breadth of experiences and potential lifelong interests.
Our pupils have opportunities to participate in educational visits including two residential stays, a range of clubs, sporting opportunities and opportunities to support and participate in community events.
Portrait Workshop delivered by Cotswolds Arts Through Schools
Skipping Workshops encouraged our Year 5 children to skip for health, fun and fitness
Celebrating International Women's Day with an inspirational presentation from former pupil and football coach Emily
Our Year 6 Residential to Kilvrough
Our Pupil Parliament meeting with former MP Victoria Prentis to discuss climate change, road safety and other important issues
Our Sports Leaders raising money for Katherine House Hospice by participating in the Santa Fun Run
Year 4 visit to local area 'The Gogs' to support their learning on Misty Mountain, Winding River
Artwork display for Dot Day
Visit to Godswell Care Home
Ancient Greece Virtual Reality experience

pageCache.pageTitle: Bloxham Church of England Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages (French)
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages (French)
At Bloxham Primary School, we follow the National Curriculum, using our own bespoke scheme to teach modern foreign languages. We use a relevant, broad, vibrant and ambitious curriculum to inspire and excite the children. Our aim is to build our children’s ‘cultural capital’ so that they are aware of similarities and differences between cultures.
It is intended that when children leave, they will have a natural curiosity and confidence to explore, other countries, cultures and languages, accepting that, in a multi-lingual society it is a valuable skill to be able to communicate effectively with others in another language.

pageCache.text:
Out of School Wraparound Care
In-house Breakfast Club
We are thrilled to offer an in-house Breakfast Club at Bloxham Primary school, providing a welcoming and supportive start to the day for our pupils. Breakfast club starts at 8am Monday to Friday and is based in the Children's Centre. The club is run in-house by staff working within the school. Cost is £6.50 per session per child and can be booked via the School Office. Staff escort the children to their registration line after the session.
High Flyers After-school Club
Bloxham Primary School is proud to offer after-school care provision via OFSTED-approved High Flyers.
To find out more, please visit their website.
Please contact them directly should you have any questions or wish to book via email or phone 07766 290242.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bloxham Church of England Primary School - PSHE & RSE
pageCache.text:
PSHE & RSE
Our PSHE curriculum develops learning and results in the acquisition of knowledge and skills which will enable children to access the wider curriculum and prepare them to be a global citizen now and in their future roles within a global community. Pupils are taught PSHE using ‘Jigsaw’ which is a spiral, progressive scheme of work, covering all of the above and 'aims to prepare children for life, helping them to know and value who they are and understand how they relate to other people in this ever-changing world’.
We want our children to have high aspirations, a belief in themselves and realise that anything is possible if they put their mind to it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bloxham Church of England Primary School - Educational Visits and Residentials
pageCache.text:
Educational Visits and Residentials
Whilst your child is at Bloxham, we aim to provide them with a range of additional learning experiences which will become wonderful memories and milestones in their learning journey.
From Reception through to Year 6, teachers plan for educational visits and visitors, which will bring learning to life for pupils. For example, pupils may visit a local farm or museum or enjoy a Roman or Stone Age Day on our own site.
By Years 4 and 6, these opportunities extend to residential visits, first for two nights and then in Year 6 for four nights.
The Year 4 residential provides a first taster of being away from home with the opportunity to enjoy a programme of fun sports and activities all within a secure one stop setting. The programme varies from year to year but typically includes activities such as climbing wall, buggy building, problem- solving, fencing and zip wire. Since 2025, the Year 4 Residential has taken place at Whitemoor Lakes, approximately 1.5 hours away. The school has currently secured future visits to this venue until 2031, with all visits booked between March and April.

Schools Outdoor Educational Programmes at Kilvrough
Kilvrough Manor, Oxfordshire County Council's Outdoor Education Centre is situated on the Gower Peninsula, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Kilvrough makes full use of the stunning venues Gower has to offer to deliver action packed adventure based courses and activities.
The Manor House can accommodate up to 60 students, on single-sex landings, in dorm rooms accommodating 4,5,6 and 8 persons.
Kilvrough, is a highly popular and reputable establishment and the school has been fortunate to secure bookings for Year 6 until March 2031.
The longer Year 6 residential stay provides the opportunity for pupils to experience a series of adventurous, high-quality outdoor learning such as caving, canoeing and climbing. Pupils will wake at 7:30 am and will be engaged in non-stop activities, interspersed with nourishing food stops until 21:00. In the summer pupils can participate in body boarding on the sea but in the winter months evening activities becoming even more exciting, with woodland walks and den building lit by head torches! This is busy and fun, but not your traditional seaside holiday!
Whilst your child is away, staff will endeavour to post daily updates and a selection of photos and/or videos to provide a flavour of activities. However, we are unable to guarantee a photo of every child, every day.
